title: Job 19
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² How long will you torment me and crush me with your words? ³ Ten times now you have reproached me — you are not ashamed to attack me like this. ⁴ And even if I have truly gone wrong, my error is my own concern. ⁵ If you want to make yourselves look important at my expense and use my humiliation as proof against me —

⁶ then know that it is God who has wronged me, who has cast his net around me. ⁷ I cry out, 'Violence!' but no one answers. I call for justice, but there is none. ⁸ He has walled off my path so I cannot pass, and covered my roads in darkness. ⁹ He has stripped me of my honor and taken the crown from my head. ¹⁰ He tears me down on every side until I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.

¹¹ His fury blazes against me; he counts me among his enemies. ¹² His troops advance together, building their siege ramp against me, encamping all around my tent. ¹³ He has driven my brothers far from me; everyone who knew me has turned away. ¹⁴ My relatives have abandoned me; my close friends have forgotten me. ¹⁵ The guests in my house and my serving women treat me as a stranger — I am a foreigner in their eyes.

¹⁶ I call my servant, but he does not answer — I must beg him with my own mouth. ¹⁷ My breath is repulsive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own family. ¹⁸ Even young children scorn me; when I get up, they mock me to my face. ¹⁹ All my closest friends detest me; those I loved have turned against me. ²⁰ My bones cling to my skin and my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

²¹ Have pity on me, have pity on me, O my friends — for the hand of God has struck me. ²² Why do you pursue me as God does? Why are you never satisfied with my suffering? ²³ Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book! ²⁴ That with an iron pen and lead they were carved into rock forever! ²⁵ For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.

²⁶ And even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God — ²⁷ I will see him myself; my own eyes will behold him, and not a stranger's. How my heart aches within me! ²⁸ But if you say, 'How shall we pursue him?' and 'The root of the trouble lies in him' — ²⁹ then be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.
